_about: Chassis. Not classes: any silhouette, any component in any slot. Every number inside a fight is single digits or low tens since the stock pass's landing (22 October: hull 20 to 50 by size, shield 6 to 16, armour 0 to 2 by role; docs/rules.md; the brief retired: git show a550c2e:docs/briefs/stock_pass.md): magnitudes, not steps, any whole number. movespeed is the move in hexes, a step a hex; water costs a ground machine two and a hovercraft or a flyer one, walls (crags, mesas, towers, cliffs) are the flyer's alone, and the way of moving among traits (tracked, walker, wheeled, hover, flyer; exactly one) is the model, the footfall and a word a passive may read, never a rule (bible section 4). size is the machine's class by mass (light, medium, heavy, assault), which sets how big it is drawn on the map and in the skirmish (bible section 7). shield absorbs a blow up to its number and the excess reaches the hull; no blow of a foe's passes it. armour is taken off every blow that reaches the hull, flat, what passes a shield included, so small hits bounce off a heavy machine; it is set by role (a tank, a heavy worker, the rest), never by size. shield_regen (optional, 0 to 9, 0 when absent) is shield regained at the start of every skirmish round, before the roll, up to the maximum, beside cooling (the long wall brief, docs/briefs/long_wall_build.md 3.6: a slot no chassis fills yet). The shield is full as every fight opens and nothing returns on the map; recharge_field is gone and the validator refuses it. cooling is heat shed at the start of every skirmish turn (0 if absent): venting is a tactic, but a round of ballistics or shields is a way of cooling too. tier is the chassis's tier, 1 to 3 (bible section 10): complexity, never more power and never the maker, so any maker may field a tier three and the capital's maker fields no tier one; a run starts with tier-one chassis, and a chassis stocks components up to its own tier, a tier three up to tier two (each component carries its own, 1 to 3, a basic a tier-one piece with its flag; the validator checks it). hardpoints is the number of free slots (and of hp_<n> pins on the model); module_slots is how many modules the chassis carries (bible section 10: a number of the chassis, never bought; two as a rule, three on the Clydesdale as its identifying feature; the runner may move the baseline for some or all); fixed lists the components built into the chassis (always on the die, never removed, no hardpoint used); loadout is the components fitted to the hardpoints by default, and a hardpoint left empty is an entry on the die that does nothing. Every component is one entry, so die size is fixed count plus hardpoints. passive is zero or one object: name and description are shown (the codex prints NAME: description), effects are what the engine runs, at most three, one idea (an upside and its cost count as one passive); the validator refuses effects the engine cannot execute. Shown to the player: codex (the inspect entry, combat and hangar), flavour (an in-world quote), the passive's name and description. design is internal and never shown: fantasy (pitch, inspiration, homages), niche (the role it is meant to fill), and notes only where the engine or a brief still owes something; the decisions and their reasons are the bible's.

tier_lift._about: What an upgrade buys a machine, a tier at a time (the bible's tiers row), its branch's pick coming with it as the choice. One standard lift of the stat lines for every chassis for now, placeholders (Ryan, 20 November: "the placeholders can be standard lifts for every chassis for now. After we have scaling in place, we can adjust individual lifts to add character"). No locked piece's number rises with the tier (Ryan, 20 November: "My hope is that they scale with either the upgrades, or with the kit. Maybe some need numbers automatically but that will be a case-by-case assesment"). The foes' line sizes tiers two and three, and these with them.

makers.name: Minerva Heavy Works
makers.style: Armour first. Everything is a tank, even the ones with legs.
makers.voice: Maintenance manual. Terse, exact, proud of tolerances.

makers.name: Kestrel Dynamics
makers.style: Fast, fragile, over-tuned. Airframes and interceptors.

makers.name: Wainwright & Sutler
makers.style: Quads and artillery. Old firm, odd designs, everything works.

makers.name: Aphelion
makers.style: Descended from the deep-space programme. Humanoid frames, hover platforms, variable geometry; high-tech suites over light hulls. White with a pearl sheen, red markings.

makers.name: The Arsenal
makers.style: The Council's own R&D house, which need not compete for favour. Heavy walkers, plasma that runs hot, big single hits, burn. Dark steel and gunmetal, black chrome.

entries.name: Honey Badger

design.fantasy: A repurposed mining vehicle, designed to take severe punishment and keep on working. Refurbishments were minimal, basically bolting on weapons and armour, it keeps most of its utilitarian mining machinery flavour.
design.niche: tanky bruiser
design.name_clash: Flagged 28 September: the id badger is Heavy Gear's Badger APC and BattleTech's Badger transport; the nickname Honey Badger is nobody's. Kept: the shown name is clear.
design.notes: Its identity settled 31 October on Ryan's go ("agreed on all proposed. Build it"; the rounds in its brief, retired: git show c05c41b:docs/briefs/minerva_honey_badger.md): the hopper the passive's business, a load for each foe a spend damages, held loads plate shown as the Ore Plate, the claw the boss chase, never destroyed a module. Numbers at the stock pass's scale: a cap of four, a point of armour for every two loads held over base armour 1 (1 to 3), Ryan's second fallback, landed the same day on the runner's read (docs/measurements.md): a point a load (1 to 5) read well past the old Badger alone, and his first fallback (base 2, a point for every two, to 4) barely moved it. Ore Hopper is a working name. Since 10 November what the loads are worth is the game's Armoured, granted by the hopper as each round opens and following the loads between, a buff a Purge strips until the machine's next turn (Ryan: "The buff he gets from it is Armoured, not an ability. Its purgeable, but returns at the start of his turn since its granted by the funnel bar"); the Ore Plate, an ability of its own, is retired.

entries.codex: The Minerva EX-45L (colloquially nicknamed the "Badger") was popular a mining mech widely praised for its reliability and durability, being designed to operate in the harshest, deepest environments imaginable. Reports exist of Badgers being caught in cave-ins while mining over 5 kilometers underground, only to dig their way out to the surface by nightfall, just in time for drinks with the crew. So naturally, when the Rifts opened, the ever-practical Minerva engineering team's first instinct was to finally give their prized Badger claws, teeth, and as many missiles as it could carry, putting its legendary longevity to work on the battlefield.

passive.name: Ore Hopper
passive.description: Damaging a foe grants one stack of Ore (max 3). At 3, base armour increases by 1.

entries.flavour: Hey Russ, ain't that yer Badger over there, covered in demon innards? I thought they retired the ol' girl!

design.notes: Ryan, 20 November: "Miner 1 - Chainsaw claw gains Penetrate. Ore max +1. Each point of ore past 3 grants an additional +1 armour. Miner 2 - Chainsaw claw gains Brittle 2, and can be used twice a turn. Ore max +2." Penetrate 2 ("2s all around"). Twice a turn, "two independent uses a turn. Its a tempo play, if the player can find the claw again": the session's reading, its first spend each turn Instant, the die rolling again, itself included.

steps.description: Chainsaw Claw gains Penetrate 2. Ore max +1. Each point of Ore past 3 grants an additional +1 armour.
Chainsaw Claw gains Brittle 2, and can be used twice a turn. Ore max +2.

design.notes: Ryan, 20 November: "Smelter 1 - Fragmenter gains Spread. Ore max +1. Smelter 2 - Fragmenter gains Ablate 1. Ore max +3." Spread 2 ("2s all around"). "Smelter 2 is a LOT of potential ablate on a spread, but thats a long slog to get 7 stacks and then wait for 7 ablate to tick down, so its a real long game chase." "The main tuning lever in my design here is Ore stacks."

steps.description: Bullion Fragmenter gains Spread 2. Ore max +1.
Bullion Fragmenter gains Ablate 1. Ore max +3.

entries.name: Clydesdale

design.fantasy: A massive, boxy, heavily armoured, and utilitarian quadruped walker, designed to fill whatever niche the team is lacking. Like its namesake, it has four thick legs and carries a massive payload on top.
design.niche: Heavy cavalry

entries.codex: Surprisingly, or perhaps not, the ever-pragmatic Wainwright & Sutler were the first surviving manufacturer to field a combat walker when the invasion first began. Not knowing the full scope of the threat, the Clydesdale was positioned as a rugged and effective jack-of-all trades, a true workhorse befitting its namesake. A hundred years later, and the original design is still barely changed, its signature W&S simplicity being favourited by pilots and maintenence crews alike. It also serves as an effective training vehicle, as its notoriously poor turning radius results in one less thing for a green pilot to worry about on the battlefield.

passive.name: Disappearing Carriages
passive.description: Its hardpoints ride two batteries of four, one up at a time: its die rolls the battery up and the Changeover. The battery up stays up from fight to fight; each battle opens on the first.

entries.flavour: Pilot manual footnotes: Most of the Clydesdale controls are just for show. The only ones you really need are accelerate and alpha strike.

entries.name: Kite

design.fantasy: A priority-target interceptor. Designed for speed and firepower and not much else, taking out a key asset and fleeing while its generous shields recharge. Since 11 November, in his word, a burst glass cannon.
design.niche: Burst glass cannon (Ryan, 11 November): it opens at double on whatever nothing has touched yet, its fitted guns its openers of choice; its lock finishes at double what is at half or less; and a kill of its own recharges its small shield whole. The first rounds of any fight and the whole of a small one; anything big after its first shot, and a long fight, are another machine's.
design.notes: Rebuilt 11 November on his words (the fast flyers' round: the bible's Kite row; its brief, git show eed817e:docs/briefs/kestrel_kite.md): four entries and no reset, the opener (multiply_printed on target_unhurt, judged once a hit), the kill's refill (on_kill refill_shield). Every number a placeholder: a paper hull, a small shield at a low regen so the shield comes back by killing, a light's heat now that no shot runs hotter; the third stock gun his to move; its mount ahead of the canopy, inset: the gun sunk level into the hull with its block hidden, the barrel out of a port into a short trough (hp_3; his, 12 November: "like the polar bear - so some of the barrel pokes out through a cut channel"; "sink it horizontally into the hull more ... don't cut a channel all the way down the nose"), the tail segment's face an air intake. Retired with it: the double on every shot, the flat heat, the dark rounds, Hot Streak and the Driver's reset (its first rework's, 21 October: git show 95d4ed3:docs/briefs/kestrel_kite.md).

entries.codex: Shortly into the invasion, it was determined that the masses of zombies, demons, and otherwordly things were, frankly, quite dumb without a guiding intelligence coordinating them. Naturally, Kestrel won the bid to produce a small interceptor aircraft, designed to eliminate priority targets and disengage before getting overwhelmed. However, the weapons package traditionally mounted on such a small frame proved ineffective to the task. It wasn't until one inspired engineer suggested cutting all 'uneccesary' weight from the design that a breakthrough was achieved; Armour, weapon regulators, ejection systems, and padded seats were all deemed frivolous, and their omission skyrocketed the Kite to excel in its role.

passive.name: Disabled Weapon Regulators
passive.description: Premium Kestrel "feature." Every weapon hits an unhurt foe at double its printed number. A kill recharges its shield.

entries.flavour: There's lighting a fire under your ass, and then there's piloting a Kite. I suggest a cold plunge before you strap in.

entries.name: Baboon

design.fantasy: A long-armed, stubby-legged plantigrade walker with a high tech suite of weapons and equipment mounted on its backpack. Not fast or heavily armoured, it specializes in battlefield control through status effects and high-tech equipment with complex effects.
design.niche: combat support
design.rework: Ryan, 11 November, its session: no tier assumed ("I never actually intended for the stingray or baboon to be tier 1 ... Let's just design the best design we can and place it later"); "I think the baboon can afford some more tools in its 'control support' toolbox. Probably go to two locked pieces, and down to 4 slotted pieces, by removing the outer hand mounts (they don't make sense with the hand shape anyway)"; its Paradox a stack a debuff stack at five, no second Paradox payoff ("it's already a pretty great payoff"); the backpack's two pods the two locked pieces ("maybe just need a little something on top, a little asymmetry"). The stock keeps the four basics on the shoulders and the fists' tops; the Twin Autoguns on the outer fists went with their mounts.
design.name_clash: Was the Mandrill (a BattleTech 'Mech that looks like ours); renamed the Baboon 28 September, Ryan's pick: a funny name for a funky machine Aphelion thought was cool. Gelada was too obscure for pilots to have coined, Silverback implied a fighter. Baboon is itself the Clan designation of BattleTech's Howler (a 20-ton light 'Mech); Ryan keeps it, a designation-tier clash.

entries.codex: Looking like a cross between an orangutan and a troll, what the Baboon lacks in speed or endurance it more than makes up for with high-tech Aphelion technomagic. After the rifts first opened (and upended everything mankind knew about the laws of physics and the nature of the universe), Aphelion set to work assimilating the torrent of new data, developing experimental countermeasures at a frenetic pace. One unlucky researcher managed to knock out his past self using a localized pocket paradoxical time loop. The effect was quickly weaponized and a frame built to lug the heavy device in into battle, nicknamed the "Baboon" in the researcher's memory.

passive.name: Pocket Paradox
passive.description: A localized paradoxical time loop, weaponized. When an enemy gains one or more debuff stacks other than Paradox, it also gains that many Paradox stacks. At five or more its past self knocks it out: every stack is consumed to grant Suppressed.

design.fantasy: A squat, heavily armoured walker with short, thick legs, its back bristling with weaponry from shielded ports that can seal for additional protection. The cockpit is tucked under the front armour, providing reduced visibility but extra protection. It seals: the ports shutter and the shell goes dark.
design.niche: tank
design.refit: Back in design since the refit pass landed (10 November): undealt until its session hands it back (its brief). Its stock is the model's mechanical re-deal and waits on that session too.

passive.name: Lockdown
passive.description: Using equipment on itself grants Sealed. While Sealed, its Cryo Flinger gains Spread. Its weapons deal +1 damage to a foe carrying Cryo.

design.fantasy: An unstoppable assault tank, complete with front rams and plows, designed for breaching reinforced emplacements - or plowing over and through fodder monsters.
design.niche: Vanguard tank

passive.name: Juggernaut Drive
passive.description: Damaging an enemy in the front rank deals 25% of its maximum HP, rounded up, to the enemy immediately behind. After gaining Barrier, its next weapon attack ignores armour.

design.fantasy: Ryan's drill-tank mole (4 November: "Some kind of drill-tank mole machine"): a low, narrow tank behind one great drill, a ring cutter turning round a rocket tip that it fires into a foe, tunnelling to it, and takes back as it burrows. Out of the burrow its cab runs out level to see past the drill's face and the fore weapon block's gun faces forward on a yoke just out of a side port and the rear block, raised on rams, fires from a port in its front over the fore one; burrowed, they tuck in behind it and every gun retracts. The name is the Thunderbirds' Mole, and the designation carries the nod (TB-2 for Thunderbird 2, FAB the sign-off): his call of 17 November, "Designation and name are good".
design.niche: tempo bruiser (Ryan, 16 November): it burrows in its reboot's place, banks momentum underground and drills a foe with it
design.notes: In content since 17 November, first so its model could be judged moving in the hangar (Ryan: "I think I need to see the model animated in the hangar to judge"); its kit's rounds and its tree's are in git with their briefs. Its numbers are the Honey Badger's, placeholders. Its four hardpoints are his (17 November: "Let's lock in 4 or 5 hardpoints for it, the drill isn't accessible while unburrowed so it doesn't add to the face count"; then "Add a gun mount to the top of the central roof, above the vent"), the top gun the fourth; its stock, placeholders: the Rivet Gun in the cab's roof, the Slugthrower in the rear block, the Twin Autoguns on the top gun and the Shoring Jack, which takes no mount, so the fore block's mount stands bare. Whatever class a mount wears stows as it burrows (Ryan, 17 November: "What happens if the stock guns are swapped out? Can't just ignore that"): the model's burrow stows any of the four in the hull under an iris, each in its port form. Its kit his of 24 November, at tier two with its tree: "Momentum is a Resource. It goes to 10"; Burrowed's turns under "50% shield regen, 50% cooling, and 50% Momentum generation", as flat numbers at half its shield, its heat maximum and its Momentum's (3, 6 and 5, placeholders); "Burrow does not bank. But it does gain the 1 Armour"; the Inertia Drill "Indirect, 2 damage (?) Rapid Ignores Armour, Ward, and Barrier. Resolve: Target gains Applied Momentum"; a burrow brings the drill back and "momentum stays where it ended up". Its directions the Glacial Mole and the Magma Mole, one step each, a tier two picking once.

passive.name: Burrow
passive.description: Reboot replaced by Burrowed.

design.notes: Ryan, 24 November: "Glacial Mole: Passive gains: Immune to Brittle. Applied Momentum -> Frozen Momentum", Frozen Momentum and Frozen as their terms say.

steps.description:
Immune to Brittle.
Applied Momentum becomes Frozen Momentum.

design.notes: Ryan, 24 November: "Magma Mole: Passive gains: Immune to Ablate. Applied Momentum -> Heated Momentum", Heated Momentum as its term says.

steps.description:
Immune to Ablate.
Applied Momentum becomes Heated Momentum.

design.fantasy: Ryan's tank that fights (14 October: a unit that "still wants to get hit, but actually has to worry slightly about its own hull"; 15 October: "We just need to make the tank not only use tank abilities"): an armoured car on six boxed wheels, his pick of 15 November ("I like the armoured car"), turning on the spot as the tracked machines do, nicknamed for how it acts and not drawn as the animal ("remember the machines were nicknamed after animals they resemble or act like"). Its spines are the Sonic Needles it leaves in whatever it strikes and whatever strikes it, his of 15 October ("Sonic Needle (sonic the hedgehog reference)"), the Knuckles in it the soft reference of his second round. The designation is a session's draft: a seismic survey car drives acoustic spikes into the rock on a line and listens to them, which is the Tether's.
design.niche: tank that punishes (Ryan, 20 November): every foe it strikes and every foe that strikes it takes a Sonic Needle; the needles conduct Chain, and every third in a foe fires Chain 2 through every conductor, that foe included; its Tether lures and saps, so the lured foe's blow is the second needle.
design.notes: His kit of 20 November, built at tier one, where it takes the Mole's place ("Now leaning T1 with this kit, would bump out the Mole who is admittedly pretty complex and niche"). Its numbers are his shape and the session's placeholders: armour 0 his, shield 10 above the tier-one mean of 8 and hull 24 the medium's ("Shield above average, hull average (as you see fit)"), move 4, fast for a Minerva (his "relatively fast for a Minerva" of 15 October). Its stock is basics since 23 November, as every tier-one die's is (Ryan: "Quite a few T1 chassis are still stocking tier 1 pieces instead of just basic pieces. Things like the Echidna coming stock with the Arc Fault Cannon and Howitzer is clearly a high performing build"): the Rivet Gun, the Ankle Mortar where the Howitzer stood, the Twin Autoguns where the Arc Fault Cannon stood, and the Shoring Jack. Its look is look A with five spines a bank, his pick of 24 November ("Go with five a bank, build the model"), its model built that day (the bible's Echidna row; the look rounds and their brief in git).

passive.name: Sonic Needles
passive.description: Striking a foe, or getting struck by one, grants that foe a stack of Sonic Needle. Sonic Needle conducts Chain. On 3 stacks, the Echidna fires Chain 2, then every stack on that foe is consumed.

design.notes: Ryan, 20 November: "Spiker 1 - Hypersonic Spike Tether: Indirect, Sap 1, Lure, Instant, 2 Heat. -> Instant allowed since its a Lure, getting hit is the point and the cost. Spiker 2 - Sonic Needle: Conducts Chain. Affected unit deals -1 damage per stack with attacks. On 3 stacks, the Echidna fires Chain 2, then consume all stacks on this foe." The Tether's new form is Instant and a heat more, named on the die; the needle's sap is Sapped's two effects on the needle itself, so it goes with the stacks a bolt spends.

steps.description: Its Supersonic Spike Tether becomes the Hypersonic Spike Tether: Indirect, Sap 1, Lure, Instant, 2 heat.
Sonic Needle: affected foes deal 1 less damage per stack with attacks.

design.notes: Ryan, 20 November: "Chaos 1 - Sonic Needle - Conducts Chain. On 3 stacks, the Echidna fires Chain 2, then reduce stacks by 1. Chaos 2 - Attacks by the Echidna on foes deal +1 damage per stack of Sonic Needle." On 21 November, of the first step: "Change chaos 1 to 'reduce stacks to 1.'" Its second step's +1 a stack is the Echidna's own modifier, read on every blow its weapons land on a needled foe, an area's among them (the pipeline's reads of a foe); a Chain's arc is flat since 21 November, and the bolt is the needles' own, so neither takes it.

steps.description: Sonic Needle: on 3 stacks, the Echidna fires Chain 2, then reduces that foe's stacks to 1.
Attacks by the Echidna on foes deal +1 damage per stack of Sonic Needle.

design.fantasy: A fast, agile, and lightly armoured skirmisher, able to skim in and out of fights with ease. It's signature ability allows it to serve as both a potent scout and harasser before getting away with minimal damage.
design.niche: scout

passive.name: Track-Dispersing Tyres
passive.description: Cannot be Hunted on the map. Hits from Brittle foes deal -1 damage.

design.notes: Ryan, 20 November: "Flakker 1 - Strikes on a Brittle foe are Rapid." changed the same day to "The first strike from this machine on a Brittle foe each turn is Rapid" ("I forgot that rapid guaranteed an active face"); a weapon's spend, its own. "Flakker 2 - Flakshot Spreader -> Flakshot Disperser: Indirect, 4 Brittle, spread, penetrate", no cooldown ("They do not keep the cooldown").

steps.description: The first strike from this machine on a Brittle foe each turn is Rapid.
Flakshot Spreader becomes the Flakshot Disperser: Indirect, Brittle 4, Spread, Penetrate.

design.notes: Ryan, 20 November: "Harrier 1 - Weapon strikes count Brittle twice." made "This machine's weapon strikes count Brittle twice." "Harrier 2 - Flakshot Spreader -> Flakshot Repeater: Direct, 1x3 damage, 1 brittle, spread", Spread 1, no cooldown. "Weaker early, stronger late."

steps.description: This machine's weapon strikes count Brittle twice.
Flakshot Spreader becomes the Flakshot Repeater: Direct, 1×3, Brittle 1, Spread 1.

design.fantasy: A small, nimble, lightly armoured vehicle designed to support heavy armour in combat. Able to stealthily avoid combat until its allies are in position for a flanking or pincer attack, then capitalize on openings in combat.
design.niche: combat support
design.name_clash: Kept (Ryan, 29 September). Dingo is a Heavy Gear Northern gear, an obscure resin-era release in a niche property and a biped, so no silhouette resemblance; the Bundeswehr's ATF Dingo, a four-wheeled armoured car, is the closer match and the homage W&S's register is built on. Say Dingo and people picture the dog: the coincidence tier.

passive.name: Retrograde Flywheel
passive.description: May move and act twice during each turn of the map phase.

design.fantasy: The larger cousin of the Kite, trades explosiveness for longevity. Wide downturned wings evoking a hovering predator, weapon mounts mounted under the wings. Double boosters mounted on top of the tail section (similar to an A10 warthog).
design.niche: A scavenger striker (Ryan, 18 November: "Do the carrion-style"): every foe that falls in its fight, whoever felled it, feeds its shield, and its guns spend the shield into their blows, a flat cost for a flat add where Empowered's goes, paid unasked when the shield holds it (11 November: "Automatically paid"), plain when it does not; its cannon fires the whole field. Its shield is its ammunition: keep it and live, or burn it into the shot. A lone boss feeds it nothing, its clear weakness.
design.notes: Reworked 18 November on his calls of 11 and 18 November (its brief: git show 288de9a:docs/briefs/kestrel_buzzard.md; the bible's Buzzard row): the Thermal Recoupler's heat regen went, its last carrier, the Storm Petrel's hook having taken heat into shield; the fuel is carrion, 2 a fall (his "I'd only give it 1 or 2 on death though, if the kills are coming from any source"); a zap or the cannon may break its own shield ("being able to break its own shield is fine"). The stock: the Shoring Jack's slot to a Barrier piece ("It should have a barrier piece instad of an armour piece"): the Blast Door, Minerva's tier-one Barrier at cooldown 1, the session's pick over the basic Halo Projector, which prints the same; the Overclocked Railgun's to a lesser warm gun ("It has a big spend with the cannon, so the railgun can be another, lesser, warm gun"), the Laser Carbine. Its branches are his (one step a direction at tier two). The passive's name is his, the same day ("The passive name needs to fit the damage-add more than the recovery portion"; "Field-Recoupling Injectors"), its line leading with the zap to match. Numbers are placeholders.

passive.name: Field-Recoupling Injectors
passive.description: Each weapon the Buzzard fires pays 2 shield, when it holds that much, for +2 on its every blow. Every foe that falls in its fight gives it 2 shield.

design.notes: Ryan, 18 November: "Sustain - The on-hit grows to 3, and the death gives 2 shield regen instead of the flat boost." The zap's add to 3 for the same 2 shield, the session's read of "the on-hit"; the fall's 2 shield in place becomes Regenerating 2, the machine half of that status he kept on 17 November for this, each slot's later grant replacing the passive's.

steps.description: Its zap adds 3, and every foe that falls lays Regenerating 2 on it in place of the 2 shield.

design.notes: Ryan, 18 November: "Burst - The cannon gains Spread and Penetrate, and either better base damage or better shield scaling (depends on how much max shield it gains on the actual chassis tier upgrade)." The tier upgrade is not built, so its base damage for now, 2 higher, the shield scaling's form waiting on it; the area's numbers, 2 each, are placeholders.

steps.description: Its Shield-burner Cannon gains Spread 2 and Penetrate 2, and its own number is 2 higher.

design.fantasy: A hulking, neckless, spiked brute. Thick arms made for pummeling. A glowing firey core in its torso that lights up as the mech takes damage and heats up.
design.niche: Sustained damage bruiser
design.one_off: Its passive's four lines (the bible's section 7): the three blows that heat it and the Rage that heat buys, one idea, Ryan's of 23 November, where a passive holds three.
design.notes: Its fourth hardpoint holds a placeholder, the plain basic gun, since the Retribution Thurible went back to design on 15 November (Ryan's word; the placeholder a session's, as a vent's slot took one on 10 November): the stock re-deal's to fill. Its Rage since 23 November, tied to heat as in its lore (Ryan: "change rage into simply generating heat, using the same rules as rage generation"; "When the Nemesis starts its turn with heat at or over max, it gains the unpurgable status Rage: Remove all debuffs on self. Immune to all debuffs. The only component available is Knuckles of Fury"; "Rage ends when the Nemesis' heat reaches zero, at which point it immediately reboots, regardless of how it got there"; "Nemesis never reboots voluntarily at max heat, yes. I would even consider not letting it reboot voluntarily at all"). The player may end the turn while it rages, the Rage standing ("I'm leaving the option open for the player to end turn at any time, the nemesis is just still stuck in rage"). If this version is too much he would simplify the heat to hits alone ("if this version is too much, we simplify it to just when hit-> gain heat"). Its rage was a store spent in fives on a charged Instant Knuckle from 11 to 23 November.

passive.name: Crucible Capacitor
passive.description:
When Hit: If only Shield is damaged, gain 1 Heat.
Hull Damaged: Gain 2 Heat.
After Hit: If damage was reduced to 0, gain 2 Heat.
Turn Start: If at Max Heat or higher, remove all Debuffs and gain Rage.

design.fantasy: A sinister digitigrade figure, with 4 clawed arms, the middle set which can be used as an additional pair of legs. A low-set snout like cockpit with burning "eyes." Absorbs energy from units it defeats with its 4 signature locked claw weapons, granting permanent overcharge.
design.niche: Scaling damage
design.notes: Reworked 12 November on Ryan's go, his own design ("The 4 claws are combined into one weapon that deals 1x4 instead, with Breach. They no longer gain Empowered on kill"; "Passive: Kills grant one Soul. At the start of a skirmish, or on kill, the souls flare, granting 1 Empowered per 5 souls"; "new locked piece: Soul Siphon: Consume up to 5 souls, granting 1 Empowered per soul. Cooldown 3"), with his calls on the holes: the Souls last the battle and carry no cap ("as part of the fantasy"), any kill in its fight banks one and only its own kill flares, once an attack that kills however many fall to it ("Flaring twice for an AoE is probably wrong, let's make it 'one of more killed' by an attack"), and the Siphon's round holds every Empowered on the field ("No Empowered decays this round. And I mean none, not ally or enemy"). The Tap's kept Empowered, its form until then, went with it: the pitch above is his of that form. Every number a placeholder. Renamed 15 November on his marks ("Passive: Quintessence Reactor. Rename souls to Essence. Soul Siphon -> Quintessence Tap. Grants the no-decay state which is represented as a buff on the Ammit called Essence Flare"): the passive is the Quintessence Reactor, its count Essence, the Siphon the Quintessence Tap, and the Tap's hold a buff on the Ammit, Essence Flare, where a chip on every unit holding Empowered had said it. The talons keep their name. The flare's second trigger moved on 16 November, his words the passive's text: "At the start of the skirmish, or at the end of a round where the Ammit killed at least one enemy, the Essences Flare, granting 1 Empowered per 5 Essences it holds." It came after each attack of its own that killed until then, and halved away the same round; Empowered halves as its side's turn ends since the same day, so the round's flare stands whole through its next turn.

passive.name: Quintessence Reactor
passive.description: Every foe that falls in its fight is 1 Essence, kept for the battle. At the start of the skirmish, or at the end of a round where the Ammit killed at least one enemy, the Essences Flare, granting 1 Empowered per 5 Essences it holds.

design.fantasy: A flat pearl-white lens of a hull that rides on lift fans sunk flush into its wings and pitches like a helicopter to move. Its heat suite is its weapon: the hotter it runs, the deeper every burn and every buff it lays. The ray's barb is its tail, lit at the tip; its lance rides the turret on its back (Ryan, 28 October: the locked lance on the dome; it lay in the ray's mouth under the nose).
design.niche: hot status amplifier

passive.name: Exothermic Suite
passive.description: Heat is the suite's power. Every stack this machine applies, to a foe, an ally or itself, is one deeper for every 5 heat it carries. Numbed excepted, as always.

design.fantasy: Ryan's Gundam homage (11 and 12 October: "a Gundam-homage walker"; "Can't be too on point ... as long as it has a shield, a handheld rifle, and a beam sword - it's a Gundam"; 14 October: "it combos, it duels other gundams, it usually SLAUGHTERS all the enemy's trash without breaking a sweat, and its theme is Beam weapons"; 16 November: "It needs its own identity", a homage, not a clone). 18 November: "the macross unit truly changes forms. Whereas the Gundam changes weapons". Its designation is his (19 November: "Apoapsis Flight 78 Partisan Frame"), the 78 the RX-78's nod, and its name ("Let's give it Macaque for now, only because I anticipate another less-aggressive walker that would take Capuchin more. If I'm wrong, then it takes it back"); the line frame was its working label.
design.niche: The agile duelist (19 November: "Its an agile duelist, not a bruiser"): a flanker that is not the fastest across the map but holds its own once there, the carry, the utility skirmisher. Squishy, its riders its power. Its offhand is the one played around beside the Macross's form, the one played towards (18 November).
design.holes: Every number a placeholder for the numbers pass (squishy: the hull and shield under the Baboon's, its move between the Baboon's and the Stingray's). The Aile Booster runs 1 hot (his of 19 November). Its branches name the booster they upgrade, the Aile Blitzer and the Aile Assaulter, on the die's readout and the codex as on the step's line (his: "I intended the gundam to change its equipment names for the booster and the offhand"). Its brief retired with the landing (git keeps docs/briefs/aphelion_line_frame.md); the bible's row holds the kit's reasons.

passive.name: Beam Armament Sequencer
passive.description: Three armaments of light, sequenced. Its offhand holds the Beam Rifle, the Beam Sword or the Beam Shield, a rider on every weapon and equipment it aims at a foe, and turns to the next after each; every fight opens on the rifle. Beam Rifle: each strike also strikes the foe to the right for 2. Beam Sword: after each strike, it hits the target again for half the strike's damage, rounded down. Beam Shield: it gains Armoured 2.

effects.name: Beam Rifle
effects.description: Each strike also strikes the foe to the right for 2.

effects.name: Beam Sword
effects.description: After each strike, hit the target again for half of the strike's damage (rounded down).

design.notes: Ryan, 19 November: "Duelist 1: Beam Sword -> Beam Saber: 'After each strike, hit the target again for full damage.' Duelist 2: Beam Shield -> Beam Buckler: 'Gain Barrier, Ward, and Parry.' ... Aile Booster -> Aile Blitzer: 'Rapid. Next weapon strike gains Indirect reach and ignores armour.'" The boss-killer, a tier-three capstone ("so it can be powerful. Also, unless it pairs the shield with a slotted lure, and times it perfectly, there's no guarantee it even works"). Each form a later grant in its slot, in its place in the cycle; the Blitzer's buff in the Boost's place (buff_status).

steps.description: Its Beam Sword becomes the Beam Saber: after each strike, it hits the target again for the strike's full damage.

effects.name: Beam Saber
effects.description: After each strike, hit the target again for full damage.

steps.description: Its Beam Shield becomes the Beam Buckler, granting Barrier, Ward and Parry; its Aile Booster becomes the Aile Blitzer, its next weapon fired ignoring armour as well.

design.notes: Ryan, 19 November: "Valkyrie 1: Beam Rifle -> Beam Bazooka: 'Each strike gains Spread 2 and Penetrate 2.' Valkyrie 2: Beam Shield -> Beam Pavise: 'Gain 1 Armoured, plus 1 Armoured for every foe struck.' Aile Booster -> Aile Assaulter: 'Rapid. Next weapon strike gains Indirect reach. Gain 1 Empowered.'" The Bazooka's numbers add to a gun's own ("Two spreads on the same weapon would combine"); every foe struck is every foe the spend's blows met, its area's included (the Storm Petrel's per target hit), since a spend aimed at one foe strikes one.

steps.description: Its Beam Rifle becomes the Beam Bazooka: each strike gains Spread 2 and Penetrate 2, added to any the weapon carries.

effects.name: Beam Bazooka
effects.description: Each strike gains Spread 2 and Penetrate 2.

steps.description: Its Beam Shield becomes the Beam Pavise, granting 1 Armoured and 1 more for every foe struck; its Aile Booster becomes the Aile Assaulter, granting 1 Empowered with its Aile Assault.

effects.name: Beam Pavise
effects.description: Gain 1 Armoured, plus 1 Armoured for every foe struck.

design.fantasy: Kestrel's one machine that touches the ground, and so the one Kestrel that can stop a pack. A short deep body in chrome on two boosters far too big for it, stubby wings, tail fins, and the whole front one shield projector, a great faired beak. Kestrel called it a very cool ground-effect escort; pilots took one look and called it the Puffin.
design.niche: The team's heat carrier (Ryan, 11 November: "it MOVES heat around"): equipment it spends on an ally takes some of that ally's heat onto it, so its own gauge is the team's clock and its reboot the team's vent; its locked piece passes its heat to an ally as power. Tier two on his lean of the same day ("I'd probably move it to tier two"), built 19 November.

passive.name: Downwash Exchanger
passive.description: Every piece of equipment the Puffin spends on an ally takes up to 4 of that ally's heat onto the Puffin.

design.fantasy: Ryan, 14 October: "a unit that sits on the sidelines, waiting to strike. Its opportunistic. We have many scaling threats, but no dedicated tank-buster, which was my inspiration - little spider takes down big thing with venom." A four-legged steampunk walker that does spider-like things (Ryan, 17 October); the lore is his and not written yet.
design.niche: The roster's tank-buster, a team machine at tier two: its blows on a foe looking away lay Vitriol (a share of current hull), the team's Lures, stuns and bare-hulled tank making its windows; its locked Web Bomb binds. Alone it is a plain d5 with a web and loses, which is tier two's shape. It waits on the elites in fights for the venom to matter outside the boss fight.

passive.name: Ambush
passive.description: Its weapon hits on a foe showing no intent on it lay Vitriol, a stack a hit; at its action the foe loses 10% of its current HP a stack.

design.fantasy: Ryan's revolver (12 October): "Whenever its die rolls, it moves to the next entry instead, in sequence." The six-shooter homage on a chicken walker: a squared cab on two long digitigrade legs, no arms, the revolver drum on the cab's flank clicking round a chamber at every roll. Ryan, 18 October: the first chamber randomized, "like a revolver spinning, the only random factor we're able to inject in an otherwise deterministic chassis". Named by Ryan, 19 October: the flightless bird that kills.
design.niche: The maker's gunslinger, a damage dealer at tier one (Ryan, 18 October: promoted to damage class). Its die never rolls: each fight opens on a random chamber and steps from there, so the plan is adjacency (the shield before the big gun, the Rapid before the chamber it should double) and the team's rerolls are its dial. Every sixth shot counts double; its locked Spin-Up spins the cylinder and primes the next shot. Squishy on purpose (Ryan, 19 October: "we're packing a lot of firepower in it"), so the maker's tender deal holds no front, accepted.

passive.name: Indexed Cylinder
passive.description: Its die never rolls: each fight opens on a random chamber, and every roll steps it to the next entry in order. Every sixth shot counts double, its damage and the stacks it lays.

design.fantasy: Ryan, 13 October: a simple hovercraft with a deck gun, and everything it fires goes through the deck gun. Ryan, 19 October: "I picture it honestly not as a deck gun, but like a big rotating set of barrels with the guns mounted (invisibly) inside, like a multi shot grenade launcher. We call it a fan boat but the profile is more sophisticated than that, it is still future-tech after all." Named by Ryan, 19 October: the water moccasin, the bayou's snake.
design.niche: The maker's versatility in a third form, of reach (Ryan, 19 October: the Clydesdale's is loadout, the gunship's stats, this one's reach), a tier one that plugs holes in many draft compositions. Every weapon it fires leaves the drum as the drum's Indirect shot with the weapon's own keywords, so a keyword shell of any maker becomes an area shot at any reach; the shape follows the aim (the back rank punched through, the front rank sprayed), so a column or a row is the decision on every shot. It spreads statuses well, which steps on Aphelion's toes and is fine (Ryan: status spread is no monopoly and no complete identity). It locks nothing, as the Clydesdale and the gunship do.

passive.name: Adaptive Munitions Drum
passive.description: Every weapon and equipment it aims at a foe leaves the drum as the drum's shot: Indirect, 4, heat 6, with its own keywords. Aimed at the back rank the shot punches through (Penetrate 2); aimed at the front rank it sprays (Spread 2).

design.fantasy: Ryan's boiler (12 and 13 October: "a crazy steampunk machine venting everywhere"; 20 October: "it doesn't actually use steam to run, its a future-tech machine. it just kind of behaves like a steampunk device"). The whip scorpion sprays when provoked. Named by Ryan, 20 October; 11 November: "this is a scorpion, so it's probably not a frontliner, thematically", and it "goes all in with the weird and wonderful, along with the cassowary and cottonmouth".
design.niche: A bursty damage dealer (Ryan, 20 November: "it's now positioned as a bursty damage dealer, but that could change"): heat is its ammunition and its risk (Ryan, 23 November: "Deals -50% damage at zero heat to +100% damage at max heat, scaling linearly. When over 50% heat, damage recieved from hits is doubled"; held at double past the maximum, his "Hold" the same day). It no longer gains heat on being hit. Its reboot fires its locked ray first, at whatever its heat makes of it, and then it reboots, so the reboot is its burst. If it is strong, he would consider doubling all the damage it takes past half its heat, so an overheat pays twice ("if it's strong, I would consider changing to all damage received is doubled, so that overheat pays twice"). A phased field leaves the ray nothing to fire at and the reboot waits ("you just have to skip or use a support action"). Its reboot's vent blasted every foe from 17 to 23 November, and every blow it took added heat. Numbers placeholders.

passive.name: Thermal Ejection Manifold
passive.description:
Weapon damage scales with Heat: 50% at 0 Heat to 200% at Max Heat.
When Hit: If above half Max Heat, double damage received.
Reboot replaced by Fixed: Heliographic Death Ray.
Resolve: If Heliographic Death Ray was used, Reboot immediately.

design.fantasy: Ryan's helicarrier: the apex of steampunk-silly military technology, a mobile headquarters on rotors that carries the squad, directs its fire, refuels it and gives it a lift. A butterfly: four wings for four rotors, big, slow, and it carries its load home.
design.niche: The maker's first tier three: a mobile HQ for strategic and tactical support and resupply (Ryan, 20 October: "a helicarrier, a mobile HQ, made for strategic and tactical support, and possible resupply"). It doesn't rain death; it directs units to rain death.
design.refit: Back in design since the refit pass landed (10 November): undealt until its session hands it back (its brief). Its stock is the model's mechanical re-deal and waits on that session too.

passive.name: Muster Deck
passive.description: Allies beside it on the map travel with it. Every die that rolls fills its Muster a sliver, a kill by its own guns more, and its Integrated components spend a muster to do more.

design.fantasy: Ryan's mobile artillery, 21 October: "a cross between a Big Bertha, a M270 MLRS, and/or a truck-mounted MEADS launcher. Big. Big wheels. Massive launchers and massive artillery cannons"; the "high-tech" Wainwright & Sutler design, "where they tried to resolve their inherent bias against energy weapons". Wide (Ryan: "Wide is good"): the old cannon on the centreline, the high-tech guns on flank sponsons, a rack of glowing cells feeding them, the musk ox's ring of horns facing out.
design.niche: The maker's second tier three, the old-world artillery and the raining death: the machine that runs on ammo where every other runs on heat, so it carries any maker's hottest energy guns without heating. Its cluster cannon earns ammo off a crowd and lays Brittle for the team; its salvo spends the whole magazine at random foes, Splash on every strike.

passive.name: Desublimation Forge
passive.description: Its weapons fire forged ammo instead of heating it: 1 for every 2 heat a gun would make, rounded up, at least 1. The forge makes 1 each round; a vent it spends on itself adds 3, a shield 2.

design.fantasy: Ryan's bomber (14 October: "a bomber of some kind", its bombs taking on the properties of its weapons: "napalm, aoe, shock, even suppress"), reworked 9 November when the slot mines failed with reinforcement gone ("A chassis based around opening an empty spot isn't a good design"): "the lammergeier basically converts all hits to AoE hits, at the cost of a delay until Death. It's the same niche as the Cottonmouth, but executed very differently." Every spend aimed at a foe leaves a Mine on it, flat damage and the spend's keywords, one Mine a foe, and when the foe falls the Mine blows round its slot. The bearded vulture carries bones and tortoises up and drops them to shatter on rock (Ryan named it 21 October): a heavy flying wing on big boosters, the mines dropping from the bay under its body.
design.niche: Kestrel's tier-three bomber: the team's kills are its area, a delay its price, where the Cottonmouth's drum makes every shot an area shot now. Every spend it aims at a foe leaves a Mine there (2 flat a spend, the keywords one big hit); the Lorentz Contractor gathers every Mine onto one foe and Exposes it for the team's Direct guns, and the Syrinx Drone sets a Mine off at once, on the foe and every foe round it. It wants keyword pieces of every maker (napalm, a shock or a stun Mine, Breach to carry the whole Mine through armour) and a team that kills where the neighbours stand. Ryan, 9 November: one Mine a spend first, "then look at per hit later if it's weak".

passive.name: Reverberant Payload
passive.description: Every weapon and equipment it aims at a foe adds 2 to a Mine on that foe, with the spend's keywords. When the foe falls, even one that gets back up or splits, the Mine blows: its damage and keywords on every foe round its slot.

design.fantasy: The strafer (Ryan, 14 October: "Love the [strafer], lock that in"), a swing-wing since 21 October, the strafing jet by trade; the Skua, the seabird that harries others in repeated dives until they drop what they carry. Since 11 November, in his words, Ramping Dakka.
design.niche: Ramping Dakka (Ryan, 11 November, a complete rewrite): the first weapon it damages a foe with each round gains it a stack of Ricochet, and after a weapon fires it hits its target again for 1 a stack, so it is the long fight's hitter, weak in its first round and a storm by its fifth, on one foe at a time. Hull damage halves the stacks, so it ramps only while its shield holds: Kestrel's risk. Its lock, the Hypersonic Swoop, is the one way to a second stack in a round. Every bounce pays the foe's armour, so plate stops it and an Exposed foe does not; its payoffs are riders laid a strike and flat buffs counted on each strike.
design.notes: Rewritten 11 November on his words (the fast flyers' round: the bible's Kestrel row; its brief, git show e5638e2:docs/briefs/kestrel_skua.md). The stack is the passive's (on_damage, once a round) and the Swoop's; Ricochet is a buff that lasts the fight, read by the hit, halved on hull damage. Retired with it: the Split-cycle Breech (every weapon hitting twice at half; the engine keeps split_strikes, which no passive uses) and the Flechette Pod as its lock, now an ordinary weapon in its stock. Every number a placeholder. Its stock is three basic guns since 23 November (his "just basic pieces" for every tier-one die), a second Twin Autoguns where the Pod stood; the Pod is a find, four strikes of 1 since Sweep went on 12 November. Its model is the jaeger of 26 and 27 October (tools/lowforge/models_low.py, skua): the belly mount wears whatever its third gun is, and the twin pods on its spine, the old lock's, are housings nothing fires until its look is revisited. Its passive's name is his (12 November: "Carom field or rebound field?", then "go for the rename"; Skip-fire Breech was a session's working name).

passive.name: Carom Field
passive.description: Once a round, damaging a foe with a weapon gains it a stack of Ricochet.

design.fantasy: The off-tank, a fast hovercraft (Ryan, 20 October: since the Puffin is slow, the shield-burner should be fast, so Kestrel is seen to make a fast hover), the Storm Petrel since 21 October, the small sea bird that patters across the water; its hard shields used both for defence and for whacking things with (Ryan, 21 October).
design.niche: Kestrel's tier-one tank by shield (Ryan, 11 November, locked 17 November): every point of heat it gains, from any source, stands up a point of shield, so its heat is its fuel and its clock at once and the overheat it walks toward breaks the shield it built; its shield armour is the Hardened Light its lock lays, a stack a spend up to 3, every stack gone when the shield breaks, a reboot's drop included (Ryan, 18 November: "It contains high points and low points and that makes it interesting and healthy. It's the only tank not weak to Expose ... since heat gives shield, heat is its gate alone, and a smart player will look for ways to support that. So it needs the clear weakness"). Its passive the Hardlight Generator and its lock the Hardlight Pulse (Ryan's names of 17 November, the Riot Field Generator and the St. Elmo's Regenerator until then), a lure that runs hot, so its taunt raises its shield through the hook. A generalist that can zoom off and fight a pack (Ryan, 20 October), the tank since its rework and no longer the striker.
design.notes: Reworked 17 November on his direction of 11 November, locked that day ("That direction is locked, or should be locked. It just needs to be finalized and landed"; the bible's Storm Petrel row; docs/reboot_machines_proposal.md): the hook (on_heat_gain shield_per_heat, a point a point), the plate (a point off every blow while the shield stood) kept until 18 November, when the shield armour moved onto the Pulse as Hardened Light (his "no innate shield armour"), the shield burn and its zap cut with their last carrier, the zap the Buzzard's to take; the lock a lure of heat 3, its Regenerating gone ("Your verdict leans are solid"); the passive and the lock renamed the same day, his. The stock's Shoring Jack, Armoured that came off only what reached its hull and made no heat for the hook, gave its slot to a gun on his "Adjust the stock as you see fit": the Arc Fault Cannon until 23 November, and since then a second Laser Carbine, the warmest basic, his "just basic pieces" for every tier-one die. Its branches are his of the same day (branches, below). Numbers are placeholders: a medium hover at 24 hull and tier one's top shield, 12. Its model is Claude's first cut of 23 October (tools/lowforge/models_low.py, storm_petrel), its fourth mount wearing its fourth gun as a refit wears a class.

passive.name: Hardlight Generator
passive.description: Every point of heat the Storm Petrel gains stands up a point of shield.

design.notes: Ryan, 18 November: "Defense branch 1: Pulse grants Ward to self. max stacks raised to 4. Defense branch 2: Pulse gains Spread, and grants 1 Hardened Light per target hit instead of a flat 1. Max stacks raised to 5." A step restates the Pulse's own grant with its cap and its per_foe, the most of each standing (Effects.self_grants). His first form of 17 November (a self-buff for a turn, then Spread with a stack for each foe lured) is in git.

steps.description: Its Hardlight Pulse also lays Ward on the Storm Petrel, and its Hardened Light holds up to 4.
Its Hardlight Pulse gains Spread, and lays Hardened Light 1 for each foe it hits, up to 5.

design.notes: Ryan, 18 November: "Striker Branch 1: Gains Chain 2 and grants self Charged 1. Striker Branch 2: Chain 3 instead and Charged 2." The deeper step's numbers replace the first's, the higher standing (Effects.granted_numbers, Effects.self_grants). The Pulse's Chain is a debuff's, its arcs a blow of the number plain and nothing else (his of 18 November: "take riders off chain. Thematically it's a lightning arc, not part of the impact"), so its lure stays on its target. His first form of 17 November (Charged 2, then Chain 3) is in git.

steps.description: Its Hardlight Pulse gains Chain 2, and lays Charged 1 on the Storm Petrel.
Its Hardlight Pulse's Chain is 3, and it lays Charged 2.

design.fantasy: The interceptor, a tilt-jet (Ryan, 20 October: "agile and omnidirectional"), named 21 October for the swift claimed the fastest in flapping flight. Two modes, and two things a round: in fast, mark, hover and vector to dodge, out fast (his picture of it), "a fox in a henhouse".
design.niche: Kestrel's tempo machine at tier two (Ryan, 11 November: "using two things a round is very Kestrel and deserves a chassis"): each round it acts twice, once with a weapon and once with equipment (the Quick-turn Avionics Relay), its die turning to an entry of the other kind after its first spend. Its Fovea Designator Exposes a foe through the next round, so with one equipment on its die it marks every round, the line's dependable setter; the chassis that cashes Exposed is one of the unspecced mediums. It wants every maker's equipment (a setter and the gun that cashes it, a buff for the hitter and a shot of its own), and it feeds the Baboon's Paradox a status a round. Beside the Kite's burst and the Skua's ramp it is tempo, and the most team-bound of the three.
design.notes: Settled 11 November (the fast flyers' round: the bible's Kestrel row; its first brief retired 23 October, git show 9ced5e5:docs/briefs/kestrel_interceptor.md) and built that day: the passive a static one_of_each, the machine's own rule and no keyword, so a Silence leaves it; one entry to turn to is no draw. Until then (his go of 21 October) equipment was Rapid on it once a round. Numbers are placeholders at the stock pass's scale, a light flyer at the floor of 20 hull, glass on purpose; two spends a round pay two spends' heat. The stock is three guns beside the Designator (the Transonic Rifle, the Laser Carbine and the Twin Autoguns, placeholders, his to name), so the Designator is its one equipment and it marks every round, as settled; the Overcharge Coil it stocked until then is a found piece again, its first build question. On 18 November, under the reboot, his two calls: the Designator makes no heat ("2 heat for an indirect expose and nothing else is pretty underpowered. It could safely go to zero heat"), and its second spend may be its reboot ("being able to do one action on its reboot turn makes sense as a niche. So it may act, and then the second spend needs to be on the reboot. Doesn't matter what the action is. It's pure tempo and flexibility which differentiates it from the other fast fliers"), whatever the first left its die. Its model is Claude's first cut of 23 October (tools/lowforge/models_low.py, needletail); its two modes' look is Ryan's pick from the fifth round's sheet (docs/looks/kestrel_needletail4.png).

passive.name: Quick-turn Avionics Relay
passive.description: Each round the Needletail acts twice: once with a weapon, once with equipment. After its first spend its die turns to an entry of the other kind. Its second action may be a reboot.

design.fantasy: Kestrel's capital (Ryan, 20 October: from irony, the capital hovers where most of the line flies), the ekranoplan, the Giant Petrel since 21 October, the family's big one over the same sea; the formation leader, aggressive where the Swallowtail is the supportive mobile HQ, pushing its allies to act and keeping the tempo up (Ryan, 21 October).
design.niche: Kestrel's action-economy capstone, the reroll economy all the way (Ryan, 20 October): the team's unspent rerolls bank, up to three; the Immelmann Booster gives the team a reroll on itself, or for three rerolls a spent ally's die rolls again and it acts again; the Spindrift Salvo's kill brews two rerolls; the Reheat Uplink Empowers an ally and rolls its die. Its own guns are ordinary; its prices are a slot, a fleet that moves at 20 and the rerolls a team needs for its own dice.
design.notes: Ryan's go, 21 October (the bible's Kestrel row; its brief, retired 30 October as its engine landed, holds the rounds: git show d84ad16:docs/briefs/kestrel_gun_platform.md). Landed 23 October as planned; its engine built 30 October (the bank, the Booster's price, the Salvo's kill rider, the Uplink's roll and the bot's look-or-action valuation), so it is fielded since. Numbers are placeholders at the stock pass's scale, an assault hover at 44 hull. The stock by kind, a tier three stocking tiers zero to two (a big flat gun, a cold rolled gun, a vent): the Overclocked Railgun, the Twin Autoguns and the Bleed Valve. Its model is Claude's first cut of 23 October (tools/lowforge/models_low.py, giant_petrel), Ryan's to judge running. After the Lun.

passive.name: Maverick's Playbook
passive.description: The team's rerolls left unspent at the round's end are banked, up to three, and spent in a later round like any reroll.
